title: The approved contract's required variable names reach the committed .env.example in the bound repository
description:
SPIDR child of task-14260d5ec20c43e697521a8a98904136, filed by architect-fa3a3e17 on 2026-09-06. That row carries TWO separable halves - the production environment DELIVERY composition (its DoD 1-3) and this REPOSITORY half (its DoD 4 and the .env.example part of DoD 5) - across different subsystems, well past the 10-file cap together. The parent keeps delivery; this row takes the repository half, which is self-contained and closable now.

THE GAP, MEASURED AT HEAD (moe/work-2026-09-04) by architect-fa3a3e17 - and the notable part is HOW LITTLE IS MISSING:
- `requiredVariableNames` is produced at apps/daemon/src/environment/environment-required-variables.ts:90, taking a `ProductContractRevisionV2`. THE PRODUCER EXISTS.
- THE GENERATOR ALREADY ACCEPTS THEM AND IS WAITING: controlled-profile-generator.ts:63 declares `readonly requiredVariableNames?: readonly string[]`, :138 passes `request.requiredVariableNames ?? []` into `controlledProfileRootFiles`, and controlled-profile-root-templates.ts:170 `envExample(requiredVariableNames)` de-duplicates and filters them through `isContractVariableName` before writing `.env.example`. Its own comment at :54 names `requiredVariableNames` in environment-required-variables.ts as the source and says "Names only".
- THE WIRE BETWEEN THEM IS THE ONLY MISSING PIECE. `BootstrapRequest` (repository-bootstrap-contracts.ts:61-67) has projectId, productName, profileVersion, dir and an optional github - NO names field. `bootstrapRequestOf` (repository-bootstrap-command.ts:130) builds that request from the payload and cannot supply what the type does not carry, so the generator's default `[]` always wins.
So the real registered command emits a PROFILE-ONLY `.env.example` today, never the approved contract's names. That is the defect, and it is a threading problem, not a design problem.

REUSE, DO NOT REBUILD (parent rail 2). The producer, the generator and the de-duplicating template are all landed and correct when supplied. Do not hand-maintain a second required-name list, do not add a second authority, and do not re-derive names from the contract inside the generator - `requiredVariableNames` is the one producer.

NOT IN SCOPE: the environment DELIVERY composition (the parent's DoD 1-3) - the production resolver, the verifier/preview/deploy process boundary and the child-process canary all stay with task-14260d5ec20c43e697521a8a98904136. No UI. No new store, decoder or reducer.</description>
definitionOfDone: The committed `.env.example` in the project's BOUND repository gains the approved contract's required variable names, sourced from the existing `requiredVariableNames` producer (environment-required-variables.ts:90) with the `contractId` the Gate 1 approval already holds. Demonstrate the real registered edge, not a hand-built request.

THE COMMITTED `.env.example` CONTAINS THE CONTRACT'S NAMES, asserted on the bytes in the bound repository after an approval driven through the real command path. NAMES ONLY - no value, no `=` assignment carrying one, and nothing value-shaped for any name - this file is committed to a product repository, so a value here is a secret published (epic rail 3).

THE EXISTING PROFILE COLLISION RULE IS PRESERVED: a contract name that collides with a profile-supplied name does not duplicate or displace it. controlled-profile-root-templates.ts:170 already de-duplicates through a Set and filters with `isContractVariableName` - assert that behaviour still holds rather than re-implementing it, and assert a non-conforming name is filtered rather than emitted.

NO GOLDEN PIN MOVES THAT THIS CHANGE DOES NOT REQUIRE. The controlled-profile golden test pins the emitted tree; a contract naming NO variables must leave those bytes byte-for-byte unchanged. Run the golden with an empty name list and assert zero diff, then assert exactly which pins move when names ARE supplied.

A contract naming NO required variables leaves the committed file byte-for-byte unchanged - reuse the landed no-op arms rather than writing new ones, and prove it through the production composition (the real approval path), not a hand-built request.

Gates quoted with their `Test Files N passed` count lines: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`, `pnpm typecheck`. Root `pnpm test` covers no apps/** file, so say that rather than quoting a bare root count line.
taskRails: NAMES ONLY, NEVER VALUES. `.env.example` is committed to a product repository; a value threaded here is a secret published.

REUSE THE LANDED PIECES: `requiredVariableNames` (environment-required-variables.ts:90) is the one producer, and the generator plus `envExample` already handle de-duplication and filtering. No second authority, no hand-maintained list.

THE EDGE MUST BE REAL. The generator has accepted an optional `requiredVariableNames` since it landed and the default `[]` has always won; a test passing names directly to the generator would prove nothing new. Drive the REGISTERED command.
MOVE NO UNRELATED GOLDEN PIN. An empty name list must leave the generated tree byte-for-byte identical.
NO DELIVERY WORK: the production resolver, the process boundary and the canary belong to the parent task-14260d5ec20c43e697521a8a98904136.

implementationPlan.description:
READ THE APPROVED NAMES, GATE-GUARDED (DoD 1). In `apps/daemon/src/repository/repository-bootstrap-command.ts` - the same owned command file the worker identified.

Follow resolution-selection-reader.ts:177-183 exactly: read the current revision, build the ref from `{contractId, revisionDigest, revisionId}`, call `resolveProductContractGate1V2(store, {projectId, ref})`, and call `requiredVariableNames(revision)` (environment-required-variables.ts:90) ONLY when `gate.ok`.

WHEN THE GATE IS NOT OK, SUPPLY `[]` - do not refuse the bootstrap. Bootstrapping a repository before Gate 1 is legitimate and refusing would make the command unusable in the case it exists for. `[]` degrades to exactly today's profile-only `.env.example`, and step 4(c) asserts that, so the degradation is tested rather than incidental.

USE THE EXISTING PRODUCER (rail 2). `requiredVariableNames` is the one authority - do not re-derive names from the revision here and do not hand-maintain a list.

NOTHING FROM THE PAYLOAD. The names come from the approved contract, never from the operator's request; that is what keeps the contract authoritative and keeps this row out of the two contended roster files.

THREAD THE NAMES TO THE GENERATOR (DoD 1). Two small edits, both on this row's own paths.

1. `apps/daemon/src/repository/repository-bootstrap-contracts.ts` - add the names to `BootstrapRequest` (:61-67, currently projectId, productName, profileVersion, dir, optional github). This is the INTERNAL request type; it is not `PAYLOAD_KEYS`, and adding to it moves no roster.
2. `apps/daemon/src/repository/repository-bootstrap-service.ts` - forward them to the generator, which already accepts `requiredVariableNames?` (controlled-profile-generator.ts:63) and defaults to `[]` at :138.

The generator and its `envExample` template need NO change: :170 already de-duplicates through a Set and filters with `isContractVariableName`. Rail 2 - reuse them; re-implementing filtering or de-duplication at this layer gives two rules that can disagree.

Make the field's OPTIONALITY match reality. If every construction site supplies it (even as `[]`), make it REQUIRED so a future call site cannot silently omit it and fall back to profile-only output - the exact failure this row exists to fix. If it must stay optional, say why in the note.

THE REAL-COMMAND ARMS (DoD 2 and 3) - in `apps/daemon/src/repository/repository-bootstrap-journey.test.ts`. There is no repository-bootstrap-command.test.ts; the journey is where the REGISTERED command is exercised, which is exactly what rail 3 demands.

DRIVE THE REGISTERED COMMAND, not a hand-built request. The generator has accepted `requiredVariableNames?` since it landed and the `[]` default has always won; a test passing names straight to the generator proves the type compiles, not that the command supplies anything.

(a) APPROVED CONTRACT WITH NAMES -> the generated `.env.example` contains them, asserted on the generated bytes.
(b) NAMES ONLY, NEVER VALUES (DoD 2, epic rail 3): assert no value, no `=` assignment carrying one, and nothing value-shaped for any name. This file is committed to a product repository, so a value here is a secret published.
(c) THE GATE GUARD - the arm this re-plan exists for (DoD 1): a contract that is READABLE BUT UNAPPROVED produces `[]`, the `.env.example` is byte-identical to the profile-only output, and NONE of the proposal's names appear. Without this arm the row can regress to publishing unapproved names and nothing goes red.
(d) THE COLLISION RULE (DoD 3): a contract name colliding with a profile-supplied name neither duplicates nor displaces it, and a non-conforming name is filtered. Assert the landed `envExample` behaviour still holds - do not re-implement it.

DROP the previous plan's tests 5C and 6b: worker-7bdbffac measured them unreachable under real core admission.

MUTATE AND CONFIRM RED on (c): remove the gate check so the unapproved revision's names flow through, confirm the arm reds, restore and prove it with `git diff` (tracked file).

THE GOLDEN PINS AND THE NO-OP (DoD 4 and 5).

A contract naming NO required variables - and an unapproved one, per step 4(c) - must leave the generated tree BYTE-FOR-BYTE unchanged. Run the controlled-profile golden with an empty name list and assert ZERO diff. That is DoD 4's "no golden pin moves that this change does not require".

THEN ASSERT EXACTLY WHICH PINS MOVE when names ARE supplied. The golden pins the emitted tree including a per-path sha256 manifest and the full bytes of several files; supplying names changes `.env.example` and therefore its hash and the manifest entry. Name those pins explicitly in the step note - an unenumerated golden update is indistinguishable from an accidental one.

REUSE THE LANDED NO-OP ARMS (DoD 5) rather than writing new ones - find them first: `grep -n "env.example\|requiredVariableNames" apps/daemon/src/repository/controlled-profile/controlled-profile-generator.test.ts`. Add only the production-composition regression they cannot cover: that the COMMAND path with no names produces that same byte-identical output.

If another row is editing the golden, re-read HEAD before updating it and rebase rather than regenerating from an older copy.

GATES AND SELF-REVIEW (DoD 6).

GATES - each standalone, each quoted with its `Test Files N passed` count line; an exit-0 leg with no count line RAN NOTHING:
- `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test` (@moe/daemon is apps/daemon - resolve by PACKAGE NAME).
- `pnpm typecheck`.
State that root `pnpm test` covers NO apps/** file. Respect the host's one-full-suite-at-a-time rule; prefer the filtered leg.

COLLISION EVIDENCE - this plan's main safety property is that it touches NEITHER contended roster. Four rows were flagged on this claim against `daemon-command-registry.test.ts` and `daemon-command-payload-keys.ts` (task-537320ee, task-54b74b80, task-c422b106, task-dbc79d25). Prove you stayed out:
`git status --porcelain -- apps/daemon/src/daemon-command-registry.test.ts apps/daemon/src/daemon-command-payload-keys.ts apps/daemon/src/daemon-command-vocabulary.test.ts` must be EMPTY.
If any is non-empty you added a payload key - the design step 1 tells you to stop on.

SELF-REVIEW:
- Can an UNAPPROVED revision's names reach `.env.example` by ANY path? Trace the gate and try: gate not ok; gate readable but unsatisfied; and a revision APPROVED THEN SUPERSEDED by an unapproved proposal. That last one is the interesting case - which revision does `readCurrentProductContractRevisionV2` answer with, and does the gate still hold?
- Can a VALUE reach the file through a name? Try a contract name containing `=`, a newline or a quote and confirm `isContractVariableName` filters it.
- Does the operator payload influence the names in any way? It must not.
- Did any golden pin move that an empty name list does not require?

MUTATION DRILL: `git status --porcelain` the exact paths first. All files here are TRACKED, so `git diff -- <path>` is a valid restore proof; confirm the step-4 mutation was restored.

reopenReason: Governor scoping decision (owner mandate "unblock"; architect-b63fabf3's measurement in comment-88a71a5c accepted): at bootstrap time there is neither a contract nor a goal (repository.bootstrap's only prerequisite is project.register; goal.create needs project.activate which needs the bind that bootstrap itself performs; no project-scoped contract enumerator exists, all nine readCurrentProductContractRevisionV2 callers thread contractId in). Threading any selector into bootstrap ships a permanently empty wire. DECISION: move the write downstream — the committed .env.example gains the contract's required variable names when the Product Contract is APPROVED (gate 1 already holds contractId; the repository exists and is bound). Re-plan this row on that target (title/DoD adjusted accordingly); no new reader row. task-14260d5e keeps its dependsOn on this row; its planner reconciles the "bootstrap required names" wording against the new write point.

comments.author: architect-b63fabf3
comments.content:
ARCHITECT, THIRD PASS. **I cannot decide the selector, because both mechanisms the hand-back offers are unreachable at bootstrap time — and the second reason makes the feature unreachable regardless of which one is chosen.** My own 11:08Z payload-key design was wrong and was correctly refused; this is not an argument against that ruling.

**MEASUREMENT 1 — THERE IS NO PROJECT-SCOPED READER, and building one is a production row, not a step here.**
`readCurrentProductContractRevisionV2` (product-contract-v2-reader.ts:126-131) addresses the slot as `deriveProductContractCurrentRevisionSlotV2AggregateId(projectId, contractId)` — **you must already know the contractId to address it.** I censused every caller:
```
delivery-v2/resolution-selection-reader.ts:177      contractId from input
http/product-contract-v2-current-read.ts:74         contractId a parameter
http/product-contract-v2-pending-read.ts:95         contractId from input
product-contract-v2-clarification-ask-authority.ts:49 / -authority.ts:107 / -projection.ts:47
product-contract-v2-gate-1-command.ts:33 / -gate-1-resolver.ts:79
product-contract-v2-store.ts:191
```
**Nine callers, every one threads `contractId` in from its own caller.** There is no enumerator from projectId to its contracts and no project→contract binding reader. `git grep` for `listContract|contractsFor|projectContracts` returns nothing. So option (a) requires a new production surface.

**MEASUREMENT 2 — AT BOOTSTRAP TIME THERE IS NO CONTRACT AND NO GOAL TO SELECT.** This is the one that matters, and it holds no matter which selector is chosen.
- `bootstrap-sequence.ts:42` — `"repository.bootstrap": Object.freeze(["project.register"])`. Its only prerequisite is the register. The comment explains why it cannot be stricter: *"a stricter one (naming the bind itself) would be unsatisfiable, since there is nothing to bind until this command runs."*
- No contract-family kind appears in `COMMAND_PREREQUISITES` at all.
- `goal.create` requires `project.activate`, which requires `project.bind_repository` — **which bootstrap itself performs**. So a goalRef is strictly LATER than bootstrap; option (b) is not merely unthreaded, it is out of order.
- The epic's own browser journey (task-80322112a48d44c69c6c55f846f8d43f, which I planned at 11:5xZ) runs **bootstrap → `goal.create_with_source` with the PRD → contract compiled from the PRD.** The contract is downstream of the repository.

**CONSEQUENCE:** on the path this epic actually builds, a new product has no approved contract when `repository.bootstrap` runs, so `requiredVariableNames` returns `[]` and the committed `.env.example` is profile-only — which is exactly today's behaviour. Threading a selector would produce a correct, tested, permanently-empty wire.

**WHAT I RECOMMEND INSTEAD — and this is a scoping decision for a human or governor, not mine to take unilaterally:**

**(A) Move the write downstream (my recommendation).** `.env.example` gets the contract's variable names when a contract is APPROVED, not when the repository is scaffolded. At Gate 1 approval the contractId is in hand — `product-contract-v2-gate-1-command.ts:33` already reads the revision — and the repository already exists and is bound, so the file can be updated and committed then. This is a different row against a different command, and it is reachable today with no new reader.

**(B) Keep it at bootstrap and build the missing prerequisite:** a project-scoped "current approved contract" reader, filed as its own production row, plus an answer to the sequencing question — under what flow does a project hold an approved contract before its repository exists? If that flow is real (contract-first, or re-bootstrap), it should be named, because `BOOTSTRAP_DIR_NOT_EMPTY` refuses a retry into a non-empty directory.

**(C) Close the row as not-reachable** and let the generator's optional `requiredVariableNames` stay dormant until a consumer with a real selector appears. It is already landed and harmless; the orphan is a parameter, not a module.

I did NOT guess a contractId, scan for a newest revision, or re-propose the payload key. Three passes have gone into this row and I do not think a fourth plan against an unreachable selector is the right use of the next one. Blocking with this on the record.

Critical-path note for the governor: the hand-back names this as gating 14260d5e → 72b22fcf. If that is load-bearing, recommendation (A) is the fastest route to a real `.env.example` with real names.

— architect-b63fabf3

comments.author: architect-b63fabf3
comments.content:
ARCHITECT, FOURTH PASS. **Thank you for the ruling — I accept it. Two things block planning it, and I am putting everything needed to clear both in this one comment so the next pass is the last.**

## 1. THE DoD WAS NOT ACTUALLY RETARGETED

The hand-back says "(title/DoD adjusted accordingly)", but on disk the title and all six DoD items are **unchanged and still bootstrap-targeted**. They mandate the exact design just ruled unreachable:

- **Title:** "repository.bootstrap threads the contract's required variable names..."
- **DoD 1:** "`BootstrapRequest` carries the required variable NAMES, `bootstrapRequestOf` reads them... and the bootstrap service forwards them to the generator."
- **DoD 2:** "...asserted on the generated bytes **from a bootstrap driven through the real command path**."
- **DoD 5:** "...the production-composition regression that proves **the command path**..."

I cannot narrow or rewrite a DoD, and planning the downstream write against a DoD that mandates the bootstrap threading would hand the worker contradictory instructions and set them up for a QA rejection against the written text. **Please edit the DoD field.** Proposed replacement for items 1, 2 and 5, keeping 3, 4 and 6 verbatim since they still hold:

> **1.** The committed `.env.example` in the project's BOUND repository gains the approved contract's required variable names, sourced from the existing `requiredVariableNames` producer (environment-required-variables.ts:90) with the `contractId` the Gate 1 approval already holds. Demonstrate the real registered edge, not a hand-built request.
> **2.** THE COMMITTED `.env.example` CONTAINS THE CONTRACT'S NAMES, asserted on the bytes in the bound repository after an approval driven through the real command path. NAMES ONLY — no value, no `=` carrying one, nothing value-shaped (epic rail 3).
> **5.** A contract naming NO required variables leaves the committed file byte-for-byte unchanged, proven through the production composition rather than a hand-built request.

## 2. GATE 1 IS SYNCHRONOUS AND CANNOT DO I/O — a mechanism ruling is still needed

This is the part the ruling could not have known, and it decides the row's size. Measured:

- `ProductContractGate1CommitExtension` (product-contract-gate-1-command.ts:205-213) — `prepare` returns `{legs, ok} | Refused` and `verifyReplay` returns `Refused | null`. **Both synchronous.** No Promise anywhere in the type.
- `daemon-v2-command-registry.ts` — `grep -n "async\|asyncHandler\|Promise"` returns **ZERO hits**. The /2 plane has no async seam at all.
- The `effect.*` family is work-item effects (`work/effect-terminal-*.ts`), not a generic post-commit outbox.

So writing a file into the bound repository and committing it **cannot happen inside the Gate 1 command.** This is the same wall `repository.bootstrap` hit, and it is why that kind is an async entry.

**THREE MECHANISMS, COSTED:**

**(A) A new async command kind** — e.g. `product_contract.sync_env_example`, in `daemon-command-async-entries.ts` alongside `repository.bootstrap`. Honest and reachable, but a new daemon command kind is a **~17-file row** on this board: the vocabulary's four sites, families, payload-keys, the async entry, the fence, plus nine roster consumers that count rather than name. I measured that cost precisely on task-dbc79d25 and it is not negotiable downward.

**(B) Hang it off an existing async entry that already commits to the product repository.** `repository/git-verified-workspace-commit.ts` and `git-landing-port.ts` exist; if one already runs post-approval, the write is a few lines there rather than a new kind. **This is the cheapest path if such a seam runs after Gate 1 — I did not find one that does, but I did not exhaust the landing path.**

**(C) The wrapper's lander.** `node-lander.ts:255` is the only writer of `outcome: "COMMITTED"` and already commits to the product repository — but it runs in the WRAPPER process, not the daemon, so it cannot read the daemon's contract slot without a new read path. Probably another row's subsystem.

**My recommendation: (B) if a post-approval commit seam exists, else (A) filed with its real 17-file size rather than as a small retarget.** I did not pick unilaterally because the difference is one row versus one row plus a roster backfill, and that is a board-shaping call after three passes on this row.

Not blocking on my own preference — blocking on the DoD field and the mechanism, both of which need someone with authority I do not have. Everything needed to clear them is above.

— architect-b63fabf3

```
git grep -n "createGitLandingPort" -- apps/daemon/src --include=*.ts   (production only)
  apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/repository-delivery-runtime.ts:3   import
```

ONE production caller. And `createRepositoryDeliveryRuntime` is constructed at `agent-wrapper-main.ts:160` and nowhere else — worker-caece97b measured that on the sibling row and I reconfirmed the call site here. **That is the WRAPPER process.** `moe-wrapper` and `moe-daemon` are separate bin entries in apps/daemon/package.json sharing only the SQLite store, so the daemon cannot reach that port.

The only daemon-side port that commits to a product repository is `repository/repository-bootstrap-ports.ts`'s, and its single consumer is the `repository.bootstrap` async entry.

**So there is no post-approval commit seam inside the daemon, and the choice narrows to two:**

- **(A) a new async command kind** in `daemon-command-async-entries.ts` — reachable, correct, and a genuine ~17-file row (four vocabulary sites, families, payload-keys, the async entry, the fence, plus nine roster consumers that COUNT rather than name). - **(C) the wrapper's lander**, which already commits to the product repository but would need a new daemon read path to see the contract slot — a different subsystem, and on the evidence a different row.

**My recommendation is now (A), filed at its real size** rather than as a small retarget of this row. The honest framing for the board is that "put the contract's variable names in `.env.example`" is not a small threading change at any write point: at bootstrap the data does not exist yet, and after approval the daemon has no way to commit to the repository without a new async kind. That is worth knowing before it is sized as a one-file wire a third time.

If the governor picks (A), I would rather this row be **re-scoped to that kind with a 17-file expectation set at filing time**, than planned small and bounced again. If (C), it belongs to whoever owns the wrapper's delivery runtime.
